# Feature: Configure Wouter Routing

## Overview
Integrate Wouter, a lightweight React routing library, into the Task Tracker frontend. Wouter provides minimal overhead routing necessary to support the new modular project management page. This feature establishes the foundation for client-side routing without external dependencies like React Router.

## User Stories
- **As an Admin user**, I want the application to have clean URL paths for different sections (home board, projects page) so that I can navigate and bookmark specific sections.

## Implementation Plan

### UI Components
- **Router setup** — Minimal Wouter configuration wrapping the main App component
- **Layout wrapper** — Top-level route provider to maintain consistent navigation structure

### Data Model (Mock)
No new data models required. Wouter operates at the routing layer only.

### Simulated Backend
No backend changes required. Routing is purely frontend-side navigation.

### Step-by-Step Implementation
1. Install Wouter: `cd client && pnpm add wouter`
2. Update `client/src/main.jsx` to wrap the App component with a simple Wouter Router configuration (bare minimum)
3. Configure two routes:
   - `/` — Main Kanban board (default)
   - `/projects` — Projects management page (created in feature 2)
4. Keep existing App.jsx structure; routing decisions happen at the top level only
5. Test that `/` loads the Kanban board and `/projects` renders the projects page placeholder

### References
- Wouter documentation: https://www.npmjs.com/package/wouter
- Client source: [client/src/main.jsx](client/src/main.jsx)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Wouter is installed and configured
- [ ] Two routes exist: `/` and `/projects`
- [ ] Navigation between routes works without page reload
- [ ] Current Kanban board renders at `/` 
- [ ] `/projects` route is ready for the projects page (feature 2)
- [ ] No console errors related to routing

## Dependencies
- **Internal**: None — this feature is independent
- **External**: `wouter` npm package
